correctness.rationale: The one-prime trace-one probability is Q/[2(Q−1)] for valuation one and 1/2 for every higher valuation. Weighting exact geometric valuation probabilities yields beta_P=(Q^-1+Q^-2)/2. For valuation below E the residue is a function of f mod P^{2E}; 2E sum deg P<d gives exact CRT independence, and two explicit couplings give TV<7d^-2. Prime-polynomial counts and Berry–Esseen prove the centered Gaussian law; a convergent renormalized product proves the zero-event constant. An exhaustive 1024-polynomial test and higher-pole checks verify finite instances; infinite assertions use complete arguments, not enumeration.

value.rationale: The motivating 2026 work explicitly needs understanding of pooled local residue conditions. A polynomial sample has a growing, nearly linearly large family of such conditions, and this result supplies a uniform product approximation with explicit d^-2 error, a Gaussian count law and exact leading probability constant for avoiding the entire mesoscopic family. The theorem is a natural, reproducible boundary between rigorously independent local jets and globally constrained residue data, useful as a benchmark for the unresolved full-pooling problem; it makes no assertion about positive orthogonal multiplicity.
